## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `fleet-joint-diversification`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-25T17:55:27.244Z.

Algorithm (24) fleet-joint context diversification — extending the catalog 2026-07-25.

Gap this closes: every algorithm in the catalog optimizes one agent's context in isolation. The workspace target is thousands of concurrent agents (pm-g2zz, pm-szv11n), and independently-optimal per-agent packing is jointly wasteful in two measurable ways. First, agents with similar tasks receive near-identical contexts, so the same tokens are paid N times across the fleet. Second, greedy relevance steers many agents toward the same few items, manufacturing exactly the collisions that work allocation (pm-3oqjnc) then has to resolve — the recommender creates the contention the scheduler must undo.

Method: lift the submodular greedy of (4) from per-agent to per-fleet. The objective becomes coverage of the relevant frontier by the union of all agents' contexts, subject to each agent's own token budget, with every agent's selection conditioned on what its peers already hold. The peer set does not require a coordinator — it is approximated from state the workspace already records: the claim ledger says who holds what, and a per-agent context sketch (8) summarizes what each has recently been served, both readable without new distributed machinery.

Fleet cache economics fall out of the same framing. If a thousand agents request context in the same minute, the honest implementation computes one shared scored frontier and derives per-agent deltas from it, rather than running a thousand independent scoring passes over the same candidate set. This composes with the write-time fold (6) and the funnel quotas (7): the fold maintains the shared frontier incrementally, the quotas bound its size, and per-agent work reduces to selection over an already-scored set.

Boundary against pm-3oqjnc, stated so the two are never merged: allocation decides which agent works on which item; this decides what each agent sees given that assignment. They must read the same frontier or they will disagree about what is relevant, so the shared frontier is the interface between them, not a duplicated concept.

Degeneracy requirement: with one agent the joint objective is exactly (4) and the peer-conditioning term vanishes. The small-end path (pm-z436) is unchanged, as the catalog requires.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
